title: World of warcraft is gonna block battle addons. Smart?

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
So, according to Blizzard CEO, battle in WoW (world of warcraft) is too hard without any battle stat add-ons.
Those community made plugins allows the player to see live stats during battle, which greatly exceeds the limited info the base game offers. Which isn't even that limited, to be honest.
Those add-ons were always allowed and pretty much every PvP'er uses them. Also in raids, where pretty much every boss in high lvl dungs are a death trap.
That has to change, Blizzard now says. "Bosses shouldn't be a puzzle". So they remove the use off battle add-ons, and if I understood it right, they will explain in-game how to defeat the boss. Either that or bosses get easier.
However... This is done for the reason that otherwise those without the add-ons wouldn't be able to figure out how to beat the bosses. Thats unfair, they say.
So far I get it. In a multi-player game, external coding should never give an in game advantage over the other player. I would think the problem wouldn't be bosses, but PvP, but that isn't the part I don't understand. This is: Why not just show those starts in-game by default?
There have always been casual and hard-core players in WoW. And even though there are more casual players today, the hard-core players carry the community. They write manual, scripts, tutorials, databases and many many more. It is rhe hard core players that keep rhe auction hall leveled and balanced. The hard-core players are the one running raiding guild with thousand of hard core member, while a rolplayer might run a guild with 10 players of which 7 are inactive or alts.
Yet it seems like Blizzard is preferring casual players. Maybe it is because they belong to Microsoft now, and Microsoft doesnt like users having control. I don't understand the real reason, but I am positive it means hard-core player will leave the game even more.
Why is this a problem? Well, let's compare WoW with RPG maker. Let's say all the veterans in the community suddenly leave, because they replace plugins with a more forced in engine tutorial. Then who's going to keep up the community? Noobs and newbies? Don't think so.
See, if Blizzard favors casual players, and makes bosses of the newest extensions easy for everyone, then noob player would easily be able to loot rare stuff by pure luck. That way, when someone wears the full set of some high tier armor, you'd never know if that is a really skilled player, or just someone who run the dungeons a 10000 times.
Okay I can keep talking about why I think it is weird that they remove something that actually made the game huge: add-ons that show you stats.
So what is an example of what mods do... in WoW the ground will show markings when an area attack is being prepared. The plugin might instantly show in text chat what those markings mean, and who's casting it. Some add-ons might even show an alert. That is info that is available for everyone, but translated by the add-ons. Others might alert when a certain boss spawns, or a quest item is dropped/looted.

posts.author: FrigidGaze
posts.body:
I'm not as tuned into WoW these days, but from what I understand from looking around, while they are disabling combat add-ons, they're adding their own built-in functionalities which reproduce a lot of what those add-ons did in their place.
Essentially this puts everyone on a level playing field, and lets them design encounters which are built around knowledge they know the players will have, instead of trying to create encounters which might have take into account if players have the add-ons or not, which creates a complicated thing of if they should make encounters appease those that are kitted out with the relevant add-ons, or make them easier so they can still be done without. But then the hardcore players will complain, and nobody will be happy, haha.
Ultimately I don't think a game should ever hinge on needing to download external tools to be able to play it an enjoyable or optimal manner, and if Blizzard is gonna try and add their own versions of those things to avoid that then maybe it'll work out for the best?
Of course, like I say, I have a very limited understanding of what is being done here, so I could be off base.

posts.author: 3rr0r1n5ynt4x
posts.body:
I usually end mythic+ seasons with a rating of around 3,5k and get cutting edge in every raid. I even have some (last minute) hall of fame entries. I'm telling that because I want to show that I'm actually a high end player. Not the best of the best, but I'm getting things done.
At least in my bubble everyone agrees that some Addons need to go / be restricted. The game WILL be better once certain COMBAT addons are removed. This mostly means weakauras that compute things for the whole raid or excessive boss mods. The game WILL be better for the vast majority of players with stuff like that gone.
However, Blizzard is going totally overboard and caused TONS of collateral damage and works on things that they should simply ignore and let be handled by the players. They are breaking so much stuff and they have a terrible track record about providing alternatives. The cooldown manager already needed a whole expansion to be somewhat usable and it's still not that great. Everything they have shown on the alpha but until now is barebones and lackluster. All of that would be ok, but they want to nuke everything once the new expansion starts without a co existing phase and that simply can not end well. They need to create perfect replacements of User interfaces, healer addons, nameplates, damage meters etc. And even then it will suck because there is only a certain small degree of customization possible.
Don't get me start on the accessibility issues caused by this.
TL;DR: Good intention, good changes, terrible execution.

posts.author: gstv87
posts.body:
JohnDoeGames said:
figuring out how to defeat the boss before anyone else does
Click to expand...
that may be true when the game is brand new, and everyone is at the same level.
but in a game such as WOW that's been running for so long, nothing prevents experienced players from hoarding the bosses by harassing newcomers trying to farm them (unless, you go with what L2 did, which was instating *instances*, sort of on-demand isolated bosses)
when games have history, there is a non-zero chance that people will monopolize bosses, which can go either way: it can create PVP and noise for newcomers, or it can lock down certain areas and scare newcomers away.
L2 also had a similar problem with plain leveling: people would use hacks or scripts to automate AFK farming.
it took the devs several iterations of protection software and moderating, to come up with the brilliant solution of adding an endorsed AFK tool for everyone.... now everyone is AFK, even at low level.... the servers are hundreds of people standing in the cities waiting for the next instance to unlock... nobody wanders the field anymore.
JohnDoeGames said:
The motivation is money.
Click to expand...
yeah... but you can strive for money without killing the thing that makes the game worth checking out in the first place.
if people decide to P2W because they find it too hard, they can still find the natural obstacle of applied expertise slapping them awake.... that's all on them.
if people P2W from minute one hoping to recover their investment and you *gift* them the investment right after they payed, you're dispensing with the game altogether.... that's on you.
if you do that, you're cementing the game as exclusively P2W, nobody checks it out because it's cemented as strictly P2W, and the game dies when the plan to cater to newcomers backfires spectacularly.
I'm telling you... I've been there.

posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
I... don't play WoW.  I've never found it fun enough to even make it to Level 10.  The four times I did attempt to play the game.
But, from my limited understanding of bosses and raids and such from YouTubers:
The game is over-reliant on a lot of third party software for "knowledge" and "boss clears".
As in, the game does a very bad (see:  Doesn't even attempt, at all) job of training its players to deal with mechanics.  To the point of needing external guides as well.  To the point that some "builds" and even "classes" are kicked from specific runs and raids and content for "not being optimal", even with the plugins that Play The Game For Them Like It's A Mobile Gacha Game.  To the point that players do NOT understand current boss mechanics, they just do whatever the plugin tells them to do.
If this is all correct (and with so many YouTubers, even high level play ones, saying so, I'm inclined to believe them), then there really aren't "elite" players in WoW.  There's just "the guys who have turned into literal robots who feed Blizzard money".
---
Personally, I like the way Final Fantasy 14 does it.  It teaches you mechanics, and future content iterates on those mechanics, or reuses them, so that players are FORCED TO LEARN how to play the game, and sometimes even their classes.
If Blizzard is going to lean heavier into that sort of gameplay, then that's a good thing as far as I'm concerned.
The company actually wants players to know how mechanics works?  They want them to develop in-game skills?  To be good, not just 'cause of external program playing the game for them, or telling them how to play, and the gear they stole from 3 other guilds before being kicked or leaving?
Sounds good to me.
Where's the downside?
